title: The Quietest Drum in Bell Bay
rule: Two lanterns facing each other create a bridge of light over the water. Breaking the pair removes the bridge.
loophole: A reflection can supply the second light. Ned accidentally demonstrated this in his shop.
cost: Rue tears the head off the ninety-year-old ceremonial drum to expose its reflective interior.

cast.want: Bring her brother back from the east pier in time for the parade.
March beside his sister on his first parade.
Keep the west lantern facing the children.
Make the opening drum loud enough to startle the gulls.
Cut hair without wetting his customers.
Deliver the island post without soaking her bag.
Get the tune started on time.

beats.visible: Flo turns the west lamp toward its mate. Seven honey-coloured boards rise across open water.
beats.line: In Bell Bay, when two lanterns face each other, a bridge grows between them. Watch the water. There it is.

beats.visible: The postwoman walks the completed bridge. Flo holds still until the last shoe clears it.
beats.line: Mum holds the west lamp for the postwoman. Turn away halfway through a delivery and the mail comes in slightly more liquid.

beats.visible: Ned turns the barber mirror. A short gold crossing appears between the shop lamp and his mirror.
beats.line: Even our barber has a bridge in his shop. It pops up during haircuts. Ned advertises walk-ins, which is incredibly brave.

beats.visible: Across the channel, Rue shows Bo the family drum. The bandmaster raises his baton on the opposite pier.
beats.line: Today was my little brother Bo's first harbour parade. My job was to bring him across and play the opening roll.

beats.visible: Quill orders a louder roll. Rue shows off the intact drumhead and Bo covers his ears.
beats.line: That drum had opened every parade for ninety years. Bandmaster Quill had one instruction. Louder than last year. Last year three gulls fainted.

beats.visible: Bo approaches the crossing. An east-pier lantern topples into the water and the span falls away.
beats.line: Bo stepped up. His flag caught the east lantern. One little clink, one very wet lantern, and suddenly we lived on an island.

beats.visible: Flo waves her remaining lamp. The dark gap stays open.
beats.line: Mum waved her lantern so hard she hit the bandmaster. Nothing grew. One lantern was still one lantern.

beats.visible: Rue reaches down at the eastern edge. Only a seashell comes up.
beats.line: I tried fishing our lamp out. I got a shell. Bo held it up to his ear. He said the sea sounded embarrassed.

beats.visible: In the barber memory Rue watches the gold boards collapse when Ned turns his mirror away.
beats.line: Then I remembered Ned. He had one lantern too. The second light was only there when he turned the mirror toward it.

beats.visible: Bo taps the worn head of the drum and points at a bright sliver of metal inside its rim.
beats.line: Bo tapped a split in my drumhead. Something flashed inside. The shell was polished brass. I had polished it every Sunday myself.

beats.visible: Rue stops, takes hold of the drumhead, and pulls it right off in front of the bandmaster.
beats.line: I could save the drum, or get Bo to his first parade. I pulled the skin right off. Ninety years of opening rolls, gone.

beats.visible: The bare metal drum turns broadside to the west lamp. Rue signals Flo to hold her light steady.
beats.line: I pointed the bare brass at Mum. Hold still, I yelled. For once in his career, Quill took that direction personally.

beats.visible: Gold boards grow outward in sequence. Bo plants a foot and walks across to Flo.
beats.line: A plank came up. Then six more. Bo put one shoe on the light and walked all the way to Mum.

beats.visible: Rue keeps the bare drum facing west and crosses sideways. Flo pulls the children onto the quay.
beats.line: I kept the brass facing west and shuffled after him. Nobody clapped until both my feet were on the dock. I appreciated that.

beats.visible: On the west quay Quill examines the empty drum and lifts his baton for the parade anyway.
beats.line: Quill inspected the empty rim. He tapped it with his baton, like the skin might grow back. Our parade started forty seconds late.

beats.visible: Rue mimes the opening roll on the missing skin. Flo beams and leads the applause.
beats.line: I still played the opening roll. Two sticks and a hole. Mum says it was the best our drums have sounded in ninety years.
